articles.title: Apple is bringing sideloading and alternate app stores to the iPhone
articles.summary: Apple has announced how it plans to change the rules for developers releasing iOS software in the European Union in response to the bloc’s Digital Markets Act (DMA).
articles.body: The iPhone’s app ecosystem is about to go through its biggest shake-up since the App Store launched in 2008. Today, Apple announced how it plans to change the rules for developers releasing iOS software in the European Union in response to the bloc’s Digital Markets Act (DMA) coming into force in March. The big news is that third-party app stores will be allowed on iOS for the first time, breaking the Apple App Store’s position as the sole distributor of iPhone apps. The changes will arrive with iOS 17.4 in March. Here’s how the new “alternative app marketplaces,” as Apple called them, will work. Users in the EU and on iOS 17.4 will be able to download a marketplace from that marketplace’s website. In order to be used on an iPhone, those marketplaces have to go through Apple’s approval process, and once you download one, you have to explicitly give it permission to download apps to your device. But once the marketplace is approved and on your device, you can download anything you want — including apps that violate App Store guidelines. You can even set a non-App Store marketplace as the default on your device. Developers, meanwhile, can choose whether to use Apple’s payment services and in-app purchases or integrate a third-party system for payments without paying an additional fee to Apple. If the developer wants to stick with Apple’s existing in-app payment system, there’s an additional 3 percent processing fee. Apple still plans to keep a close eye on the app distribution process. All apps must be “notarized” by Apple, and distribution through third-party marketplaces is still managed by Apple’s systems. Developers will only be allowed to distribute a single version of their app across different app stores, and they’ll still have to abide by some basic platform requirements, like getting scanned for malware. The new cost of doing business Going forward, developers could pay no commission to Apple at all in the EU, depending on how they choose to distribute their apps. Apple is making changes to how its fee structures work, both in the App Store and for apps newly distributed outside of it. Developers can either choose to use these new business terms or stick with the existing model and continue to distribute through the App Store as normal. Under the new terms, apps distributed through the App Store that choose to use an alternative payment system will pay a 17 percent commission (rather than 30 percent) on digital goods and services. This commission rate falls to 10 percent for any apps that currently qualify for Apple’s reduced “small business” rate. The additional 3 percent fee then applies for developers that choose to use Apple’s payment processing system. The company is also introducing a new type of fee for particularly popular apps. The new Core Technology Fee will charge developers €0.50 (around 54 cents) per annual app install; however, this fee only kicks in after a million annual installs in the EU. Apple estimates that over 99 percent of developers will either “reduce or maintain the fees they owe to Apple” under the new business terms and that “less that 1 percent” of developers would pay a core technology fee. As well as allowing alternative app stores and payment systems, Apple is also opening up other aspects of the iOS ecosystem in the EU. Alternative browser engines to WebKit will be allowed for the first time, and users will get a choice of alternative browsers to install when they open up Safari for the first time on iOS 17.4. The App Store itself is also opening up to allow game streaming services globally, which, until now, have been all but banned under Apple’s existing policies. As announced last week by the European Commission, Apple is also preparing to allow developers in the European Economic Area to offer NFC payments in their third-party apps. The DMA effect These changes are likely to be seized upon by developers that have been critical of Apple’s control over iOS app distribution. Earlier this week, Spotify — a longtime critic of Apple’s 30 percent commission rate — announced plans to bring in-app purchases back to its iOS app to let users upgrade subscriptions or buy audiobooks in the EU after the DMA comes into force. But it’s unclear whether the company will be happy to continue to pay a 17 percent commission to Apple if it’s using an alternative payment processor — it has already been critical of Apple’s plans to charge a 27 percent commission on alternative payments in the US. Passed in 2022, the DMA is the EU’s strongest attempt yet to rein in the alleged anticompetitive practices of Big Tech companies, which the regulation refers to as “gatekeepers.” The EU designated Apple as a gatekeeper last September and listed its App Store, Safari browser, and iOS operating system as “core platform services” that would have to comply with the DMA’s rules. The European Commission declined to comment on today’s announcements by Apple. The regulation is broad, but it includes obligations around letting users install third-party apps or app stores, uninstall stock apps, and change default services; making large messaging services interoperable with rivals; and banning gatekeepers from ranking their own products higher in app stores than third-party rivals or requiring app developers to use a gatekeeper’s in-app payment system. As well as designating iOS, Safari, and the App Store as core platform services, the European Commission also opened an investigation into whether iMessage should be included (which would include having to make it interoperable with rivals), but reports suggest it might avoid being designated, and today’s announcement from Apple makes no mention of changes coming to iMessage. As well as Apple, the European Commission also designated Amazon, Meta, and Microsoft, alongside TikTok parent ByteDance and Google parent Alphabet, as gatekeepers under the DMA. Several of the companies, including Meta, Google, and Microsoft, have publicly announced upcoming changes to their services as a result of the regulation. Alongside iOS, Google’s Android operating system has also been designated as a core platform service under the DMA, but it’s likely to have to make fewer changes than iOS given it technically already allows sideloading and third-party app stores (even if its policies around them have proved contentious). Apple has continued to take a cut when it’s been forced to allow third-party payments in the past. In response to a US ruling that said Apple had to allow links to outside payments, the iPhone maker said it would allow developers to link out but said it would continue to charge a 27 percent commission (as opposed to 30 percent). It’s also taken a similar approach in South Korea and the Netherlands. We’ll have to wait and see whether Apple’s changes, including its new commission rates, will satisfy its loudest critics, such as Spotify and Epic Games, which have fought hard against the so-called “Apple Tax.” But after years of theoretical debates and hard-fought court arguments, we’re about to find out whether users, at least in the EU, care as much about alternative app stores and payment methods or whether they’ll choose to stick with Apple’s in-house options. Update January 25th, 2:25PM ET: Added mention of the European Commission declining to comment.

articles.title: Chrome is about to show even more safety warnings
articles.summary: Google Chrome will start asking users for their permission before accessing a website without HTTPS by default, starting with the release of Chrome 154 in October 2026.
articles.body: You’re going to start seeing more warnings in Chrome when accessing insecure sites. Starting next October, Chrome will soon warn users when they visit a public website without an encrypted HTTPS connection. Chrome already issues a “Your connection is not private” message when you visit pages that have an HTTPS connection that’s misconfigured. But this will expand the warnings to websites that don’t use HTTPS at all. Google first offered insecure connections warnings for HTTP pages in 2021, but users had to opt in to see them. HTTPS — or Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure — uses encryption to establish a secure connection with a website, preventing bad actors from snooping on the private information you enter. [Image: HTTPS connections now make up around 95 to 99 percent of connections, Google says. “This level of adoption is what makes it possible to consider stronger mitigations against the remaining insecure HTTP,” Google writes in its announcement. The company notes that “the largest contributor to insecure HTTP” is private websites, adding that it remains complicated for them to get an HTTPS certification. “HTTP navigations to private sites can still be risky, but are typically less dangerous than their public site counterparts because there are fewer ways for an attacker to take advantage of these HTTP navigations,” Google says. Before making HTTPS the default for everyone, Google plans on rolling out the change to people who have enabled Enhanced Safe Browsing protections in Chrome starting in April 2026. Google adds that users will still be able to disable HTTP warnings by turning off the “Always Use Secure Connections” setting.

articles.title: Apple opens iOS to third-party app stores in Japan
articles.summary: It will also allow third-party payment processing and web purchases, though with new fees to compensate.
articles.body: Apple has announced the changes it’s making to the iOS App Store in Japan in order to comply with recent legislation in the country. It will allow third-party app stores and payment processing options, though is introducing new commission fees for those transactions. Developers in Japan will now be able to distribute apps on alternative app stores, much like in the EU, with AltStore PAL already expecting to launch in the country before the year’s end. As in Europe, Apple will collect a 5 percent commission for in-app purchases made in third-party stores. App Store apps will also now be permitted to use alternative payment options alongside Apple’s, or link out to websites where users can make purchases. Apple will still charge up to 21 percent per transaction for in-app purchases, with a 15 percent commission for digital goods bought through a website linked from the app. Apple will include warnings to users when using third-party stores or alternative payment options. Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney pointed to those warnings, and Apple’s commission fees, when confirming that Fortnite won’t yet return to iOS in Japan. Similar warnings and fees have been at issue in the US, where Apple recently lost an appeal in its ongoing antitrust dispute with Epic.

articles.title: Acidente Voepass: quem são os 12 réus denunciados pelo desastre aéreo que matou 62 pessoas em Vinhedo | G1
articles.standfirst: Justiça Federal aceitou a denúncia do MPF e 12 pessoas vão responder por crimes de atentado contra a segurança do transporte aéreo e sinistro em transporte aéreo.
articles.summary: Justiça Federal aceitou a denúncia do MPF e 12 pessoas vão responder por crimes de atentado contra a segurança do transporte aéreo e sinistro em transporte aéreo.
articles.body:
Escombros de avião em Vinhedo (SP) neste sábado, dia 10 de agosto de 2024 — Foto: Nelson Almeida/AFP

Profissionais com experiência e formação no setor da aviação e engenharia aeronáutica estão entre os 12 funcionários e executivos da Voepass denunciados pelo Ministério Público Federal (MPF) pelo desastre aéreo que matou 62 pessoas em agosto de 2024, em Vinhedo (SP).

O MPF informou, nesta quarta-feira (21), que a denúncia foi aceita pela Justiça Federal, e os 12 denunciados se tornaram réus. Eles vão responder por crimes de atentado contra a segurança do transporte aéreo e sinistro em transporte aéreo.

➡ Sinistro é a queda, destruição ou grave comprometimento de algum meio de transporte marítimo, fluvial ou aéreo. No caso do acidente em Vinhedo, se enquadra como um sinistro em transporte aéreo por queda ou destruição de aeronave. O Código Penal prevê pena de reclusão, de quatro a doze anos.

Entre os responsabilizados estão o dono da companhia de Ribeirão Preto (SP), José Luis Felicio Filho, e o diretor de manutenção Eric Cônsoli , apontado por ex-funcionários como uma figura de grande influência dentro da empresa antes da crise provocada pela queda do avião e do encerramento das atividades.

🔎 O atentado contra a segurança do transporte aéreo é previsto no artigo 261 do Código Penal. O crime ocorre quando alguém expõe a perigo uma aeronave ou dificulta, ou impede a navegação aérea. A pena prevista é de 2 a 5 anos de prisão. Se do fato resulta a queda ou destruição da aeronave, a pena passa para 4 a 12 anos. Se houver morte, a pena pode ser aplicada em dobro.

Nos tópicos a seguir, veja quem são os denunciados pelo MPF após a queda do voo 2283 :

Arte mostra quem são os 12 denunciados pelo MPF após queda do voo 2283 em Vinhedo (SP) — Foto: Arte/g1

Comandante Felício, presidente da Voepass, em primeiro pronunciamento após acidente — Foto: Reprodução/Voepass

Empresário e piloto comercial há mais de 30 anos, é o proprietário e o principal gestor da companhia desde os anos 2000, quando o pai, fundador da empresa, antiga Passaredo Transportes Aéreos, deixou o comando.

Ao assumir o controle acionário e a gestão executiva da Passaredo, liderou reestruturações importantes, como o processo de recuperação judicial entre 2012 e 2017 e a aquisição da MAP Linhas Aéreas em 2019, quando a marca foi reformulada para Voepass. Após a tragédia em Vinhedo, voltou à liderança executiva direta da empresa, exonerando diretores.

Como diretor presidente e acionista majoritário, foi indiciado por ter ciência da cultura de omissão . Em termos práticos, essa omissão dolosa, segundo a PF, permitiu que aeronaves inseguras operassem em rotas com previsão de gelo severo.

Marcel Moura, diretor da de operações Voepass — Foto: Acervo/EP

Com experiência como piloto comercial e como instrutor, era o diretor de operações da companhia aérea do interior de São Paulo. Natural de Chapecó (SC), iniciou o curso de piloto em 1994 e ingressou na aviação comercial em 2000.

Possui 30 anos de experiência, tendo atuado como copiloto, comandante, instrutor de voo e examinador. Trabalhou por 14 anos em uma fabricante de aviões brasileira, com experiência em voos internacionais em diversos países.

Ingressou na Voepass em 2022, a convite do presidente da empresa, na diretoria de operações, departamento que tinha a função de assegurar que todos os procedimentos estivessem em conformidade com as legislações e protocolos nacionais e internacionais.

Foi indiciado por não garantir que as operações seguissem as normas de segurança. Como gestor, era o responsável por setores que ignoraram restrições técnicas graves da aeronave acidentada , tendo inclusive respondido pessoalmente à Anac sobre falhas anteriores no mesmo avião, segundo a PF.

Raphael Limongi de Figueiredo, indiciado no inquérito da PF sobre a queda do voo 2283 da Voepass — Foto: Reprodução

Com mais de 15 anos de experiência na aviação civil nacional e internacional, foi chefe dos pilotos da Voepass até o fim de julho de 2024, quando foi substituído por Rafael Gimenez Rodrigues.

Antes, também atuou como gestor da divisão de Garantia de Qualidade Operacional de Voo. Com a exoneração de Marcel Moura em setembro de 2024, Limongi foi alçado ao posto de diretor de Operações da Voepass.

Segundo a Polícia Federal, é suspeito de usar a autoridade que tinha para forçar a operação de aeronaves inoperantes .

Rafael Gimenez Rodrigues, indiciado no inquérito da PF sobre a queda do voo 2283 da Voepass — Foto: Reprodução

Nomeado chefe dos pilotos no fim de julho de 2024 , era encarregado de acompanhar os padrões de padronização operacional e escalas dos profissionais da companhia.

Formado em 2021 em ciências aeronáuticas em Santa Catarina, escreveu na conclusão de curso uma monografia analisando fatores de risco associados à jornada de trabalho de tripulantes técnicos e a prevenção de acidentes aeronáuticos.

Foi indiciado por participar da omissão sistêmica de reportes de panes e pela promoção irregular de comandantes sem experiência mínima exigida .

Eric Cônsoli, indiciado pela PF no inquérito da queda do voo 2283 da Voepass — Foto: Reprodução/Linkedin

Engenheiro aeronáutico formado em 2002, ingressou em 2010 na Passaredo (antigo nome da Voepass), onde ocupou os cargos de diretor de Frota, Logística e compras, além de diretor de manutenção da companhia , posição que deixou em setembro de 2024, após 15 anos à frente da área, quando foi um dos demitidos por Felício após o desastre aéreo.

Segundo ex-funcionários da companhia, Eric era uma figura de grande influência dentro da companhia.

Ele foi um dos executivos da companhia a prestar depoimento em uma comissão aberta na Câmara dos Deputados, em 2024, para investigar o acidente. Na oportunidade, ele afirmou que sempre trabalhou para garantir que todas as aeronaves voassem com 100% de condição de navegabilidade, seguindo rigorosamente os manuais dos fabricantes e as regras dos órgãos reguladores.

Na época, ele também garantiu que a empresa passava por inspeções periódicas da Anac e por auditorias externas voluntárias da IATA.

Segundo registros fiscais, Eric Cônsoli é dono da RP Aviation, criada em julho de 2025 e com funcionamento no mesmo hangar que antes era da Voepass. Segundo dados da Receita Federal, a empresa é de atividades auxiliares dos transportes aéreos, exceto operação dos aeroportos e campos de aterrissagem.

No entendimento da PF, ele foi identificado como um dos diretores que ligavam para as equipes de pista para pressionar pela liberação de aviões inoperantes.

David da Costa Faria Neto, indiciado no inquérito da PF sobre a queda do voo 2283 da Voepass — Foto: Reprodução

Com mais de 50 anos de aviação, iniciou a carreira na Força Aérea Brasileira (FAB) aos 15 anos, onde permaneceu por 30 anos. Além disso, trabalhou na Agência Nacional de Aviação Civil por quatro anos.

Na Voepass, atuou como diretor de Segurança Operacional da Voepass de 2016 até setembro de 2024 , quando foi demitido por Felício.

Ele também foi um dos representantes da empresa que, em 2024, prestou depoimento a uma comissão na Câmara dos Deputados, ocasião em que confirmou ter participado de todas as tratativas de apoio aos familiares das vítimas e reiterou boas práticas da empresa com relação à manutenção das aeronaves.

Faria Neto foi indiciado por permitir que o sistema de gerenciamento de segurança operacional funcionasse sem efetividade prática de investigação . Na prática, segundo a PF, a diretoria falhou ao não identificar nem corrigir a sistemática de não se reportar falhas , o que foi central para a queda da aeronave.

Tiago Passucci Morani, indiciado no inquérito da PF sobre a queda do voo 2283 da Voepass — Foto: Reprodução

Com formação técnica em manutenção aeronáutica, era o inspetor chefe da companhia e credenciado pela Anac para liberar as aeronaves ATR 72 e a atestar suas condições de uso.

O nome dele também consta como sócio-administrator de empresas nas áreas de comércio e importação e de serviços administrativos.

Morani assinou liberações técnicas de aeronaves sem possuir a habilitação exigida e estava ciente das panes crônicas no sistema de degelo, de acordo com a PF.

Marcos Hiroyuki Sato, indiciado no inquérito da PF sobre a queda do voo 2283 da Voepass — Foto: Reprodução

Era despachante operacional de voo e foi indiciado por autorizar o despacho da aeronave no voo do acidente contrariando regras objetivas da MEL sobre o limpador de para-brisa inoperante.

Alex de Souza Leandro, indiciado no inquérito da PF sobre a queda do voo 2283 da Voepass — Foto: Reprodução

Técnico de manutenção da Voepass, ele assinou o fechamento da lista de ações corretivas retardadas (ACR) e o "daily check" (inspeção diária) da aeronave no dia 9 de agosto de 2024.

O laudo observa que, nas fichas por ele assinadas, não constavam as falhas de degelo ocorridas nos voos anteriores daquele mesmo dia, pois não haviam sido lançadas pelos pilotos.

Ele foi indiciado por assinar a liberação técnica da aeronave sem realizar os testes obrigatórios e ignorando alertas verbais diretos sobre falhas no sistema de degelo . Assim, segundo a PF, ele permitiu que o avião operasse com um sistema crítico inoperante para ceder à pressão de não atrasar a malha aérea.

William Schmidt Agatz, indiciado no inquérito da PF sobre a queda do voo 2283 da Voepass — Foto: Reprodução

Agatz era gerente do centro de controle operacional da Voepass e considerado uma peça central na cadeia de decisão das operações, como um elo entre a diretoria, o centro de controle de manutenção e os despachantes para decidir quais aeronaves operariam ou seriam retidas para manutenção.

Segundo a PF, Agatz sabia da prática sistemática de mascarar falhas técnicas, mas se omitiu por não impedir a liberação das aeronaves, mesmo também tendo poder decisório.

Juliano Flores Pacheco, indiciado no inquérito da PF sobre a queda do voo 2283 da Voepass — Foto: Reprodução

Atuava como gerente do centro de controle de manutenção , sendo o superior direto dos mecânicos de pista. Mesmo com sua licença de mecânico cassada pela Anaca desde 2022 por irregularidades técnicas, ele continuava na chefia do setor.

Segundo a apuração da PF, Pacheco exercia pressão sobre mecânicos para liberarem aeronaves com defeitos e autorizou liberações baseadas em capítulos falsos da Lista de Equipamentos Mínimos para forçar voos irregulares.

Carlos Alberto Costa, indiciado no inquérito da PF sobre a queda do voo 2283 da Voepass — Foto: Reprodução

Costa era diretor de manutenção da companhia, integrando a alta direção técnica, e era o responsável pela supervisão direta do centro de controle de manutençãoi e do setor de confiabilidade (SASC).

Segundo a PF, ele foi indiciado por omissão na posição de garantidor da segurança da frota, permitindo que deficiências crônicas como as falhas no sistema de degelo fossem mascaradas por manipulações de procedimentos, renovações artificiais de prazos de manutenção e até o uso de peças de sucata para simular trocas de componentes.

O que disseram os indiciados durante as investigações

A reportagem não conseguiu falar com as defesas dos indiciados até a última atualização desta notícia. Veja o que eles disseram durante as investigações da Polícia Federal:

José Luiz Felício Filho : admitiu ter ciência da cultura de omissão de reportes de panes, revelando inclusive que diretores da Anac o alertaram pessoalmente sobre esse padrão de conduta dos pilotos ao longo dos anos.

Ele também reconheceu que a aeronave não deveria estar nas condições técnicas em que se encontrava, nem deveria ter sido despachada para aquela rota, embora tenha alegado que sua equipe de segurança operacional trabalhava apartada das decisões diárias.

Marcos Hiroyuki Sato : justificou o despacho da aeronave com o limpador de para-brisa inoperante alegando que o aeródromo alternativo não tinha previsão de chuva, mas admitiu que autorizou o voo para evitar transtornos logísticos e financeiros à Voepass, pois manter o avião parado em Cascavel causaria um cancelamento de pelo menos 12 horas por falta de tripulação no local.

Alex de Souza Leandro: negou ter recebido qualquer relato verbal de seus auxiliares sobre a pane no sistema de degelo reportada pelo comandante Serra na madrugada do acidente. Apesar de ter assinado a liberação da aeronave no "daily check", alegou que, como o piloto não havia feito anotações formais no livro, a aeronave estava apta para o serviço, versão que foi contestada pelos testemunhos de seus subordinados.

Raphael Limongi de Figueiredo : negou em depoimento ter conhecimento das falhas intermitentes no sistema de degelo da aeronave antes do acidente.

Marcel Sarquis Moura : alegou em sua defesa que sua função na diretoria era apenas prover facilidades logísticas, e que a responsabilidade técnica pelas operações e tripulações cabia ao piloto chefe.

'Não reportar': áudio de ex-piloto mostra rotina para não relatar panes na Voepass — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

Em nota enviada nesta quarta-feira (21), a Voepass afirmou que manteve a segurança operacional como princípio fundamental ao longo de mais de três décadas de atuação na aviação brasileira. Disse também que seguirá colaborando com o Poder Judiciário e demais autoridades competentes. Leia na íntegra abaixo:

"A VOEPASS entende que, com o recebimento da denúncia pela Justiça Federal, o processo seguirá os trâmites previstos em lei, assegurando às partes envolvidas.

A companhia seguirá colaborando com o Poder Judiciário e com as demais autoridades competentes, fornecendo os documentos e as informações que forem solicitadas ao longo do processo.

Ao longo de mais de três décadas de atuação na aviação brasileira, a VOEPASS manteve a segurança operacional como princípio fundamental, com procedimentos de manutenção, operação e treinamento orientados pela regulamentação aeronáutica e por suas diretrizes internas de segurança e conformidade.

A defesa de José Luiz Felício Filho informa que tomou conhecimento do recebimento, pela Justiça Federal, da denúncia apresentada pelo Ministério Público Federal e que se manifestará nos autos, no momento adequado, exercendo plenamente as garantias constitucionais do contraditório, da ampla defesa e do devido processo legal.

À época do acidente com o voo 2283, Felício integrava o Conselho da VOEPASS e estava afastado da gestão direta e cotidiana da operação, tendo retomado a gestão executiva após o acidente.

Felício tem colaborado com as autoridades desde o início das apurações e seguirá à disposição da Justiça para contribuir com o completo esclarecimento dos fatos.

O executivo mantém sua confiança no devido processo legal e reitera seu respeito às autoridades e sua solidariedade aos familiares das vítimas do voo 2283."

articles.title: Governos e empresas tiram sites do ar após descoberta de falhas que facilitam ataques hackers | G1
articles.standfirst: Vulnerabilidades na linguagem de programação PHP podem permitir que hackers invadam servidores sem precisar de senha. Autoridades de segurança recomendaram a atualização imediata dos sistemas ou a suspensão dos serviços afetados.
articles.summary: Autoridades de segurança recomendaram a atualização imediata dos sistemas ou a suspensão dos serviços afetados.
articles.body:
Agências governamentais e empresas em diferentes países tiraram sites do ar nesta quarta-feira (21) após a descoberta de duas falhas críticas relacionadas ao PHP, linguagem de programação utilizada em grande parte dos sites da internet

A Agência de Segurança Nacional dos Estados Unidos (NSA) pediu que as organizações corrigissem as falhas imediatamente ou desligassem os sistemas vulneráveis.

As falhas "frequentemente proporcionam um caminho direto para o sistema de arquivos ou para o banco de dados do servidor", afirmou a NSA em um comunicado no X.

Hackers poderiam explorar essas vulnerabilidades para assumir o controle de servidores de sites sem precisar de senha.

O PHP é usado em plataformas populares de criação de sites, o que significa que as falhas podem afetar uma grande variedade de páginas na internet, de lojas online e veículos de notícias a serviços governamentais.

A descoberta ocorreu em meio ao auge de divulgações sobre segurança de software impulsionado por modelos de inteligência artificial (IA) cada vez mais poderosos.

Mantida a tendência atual, o número de vulnerabilidades detectadas em 2026 pode dobrar o recorde alcançado no ano passado.

Desenvolvedores voluntários do projeto PHP lançaram uma atualização para corrigir as falhas nesta quarta-feira (21).

"Se você usa PHP, é imperativo atualizá-lo imediatamente", afirmou a PHP Foundation, que financia os desenvolvedores que trabalham na linguagem.

As falhas foram reportadas em agosto pela empresa de segurança Calif e pela OpenAI, criadora do ChatGPT, que as identificou de forma independente no mesmo dia. Posteriormente, a Wiz, empresa de segurança na nuvem pertencente ao Google, informou ter encontrado outras maneiras de explorar as vulnerabilidades.

Naquele momento, elas foram comunicadas de forma privada aos desenvolvedores do PHP e mantidas em sigilo enquanto se preparava uma correção.

Os detalhes vazaram online na terça-feira, um dia antes do lançamento previsto, o que desencadeou uma corrida contra o tempo para tirar sites do ar.

Na França, sites de administrações locais, incluindo o da Prefeitura de Polícia de Paris, estão inacessíveis desde a tarde desta quarta-feira a pedido da Agência Nacional de Cibersegurança francesa, após a "detecção de uma vulnerabilidade crítica de segurança", informou o Ministério do Interior.

Nos Países Baixos, o serviço nacional de identidade digital DigiD, o site da Câmara dos Representantes e o do centro nacional de cibersegurança foram desligados como medida de precaução, de acordo com a emissora pública holandesa NOS.

articles.title: Setor de farmácia é interditado durante operação no Sertão da PB; Supermercado e postos são autuados | G1
articles.standfirst: Fiscalização foi feita em conjunto pelo Ministério Público da Paraíba (MPPB) e outros órgãos, em Piancó. Ao todo, nesta quarta-feira (21), cinco estabelecimentos foram fiscalizados.
articles.summary: Fiscalização foi feita em conjunto pelo Ministério Público da Paraíba (MPPB) e outros órgãos, em Piancó. Ao todo, nesta quarta-feira (21), cinco estabelecimentos foram fiscalizados.
articles.body:
Setor de farmácia é interditado durante operação no Sertão da PB; Supermercado e postos são autuados — Foto: MPPB

Uma operação conjunta do Programa de Proteção e Defesa do Consumidor do Ministério Público da Paraíba (MP-Procon) e de vários órgãos interditou o ambulatório de uma farmácia, além de autuar um supermercado e dois postos de gasolina , na cidade de Piancó , no Sertão do estado, nesta quarta-feira (21). Os nomes dos estabelecimentos não foram divulgados .

De acordo com o MP-Procon, na farmácia que teve interditado o ambulatório, foram encontradas irregularidades como:

Ausência de autorização sanitária para a prestação de serviços farmacêuticos;

Produtos expostos à venda sem indicação de preços;

Ausência de informação clara sobre a proibição de exigir CPF como condição para a concessão de descontos;

Falta de exemplar do Código de Defesa do Consumidor (CDC) em local visível e acessível ao público.

Na farmárcia, medicamentos manipulados também foram apreendidos. Entre as irregularidades sanitárias, foram identificados medicamentos sujeitos a controle especial sem a devida escrituração no sistema de controle de produtos, incluindo canetas emagrecedoras.

No supermercado autuado, a fiscalização notou a ausência de apresentação do certificado do Corpo de Bombeiros dentro da validade, além da existência de produtos sem data de validade, rótulo ou informações que permitissem a rastreabilidade.

Também foram encontrados alimentos com prazo de validade vencido, presença de mofo e características sensoriais alteradas , tornando-os impróprios para o consumo. As equipes verificaram ainda condições inadequadas de higiene nos locais de manipulação e armazenamento de alimentos, em desacordo com as normas sanitárias vigentes.

Em relação aos postos de combustíveis autuados outras irregularidades foram identificadas. No primeiro posto fiscalizado, a equipe constatou a ausência do cartaz obrigatório sobre a proibição de discriminação por orientação sexual. No local, foi identificada a falta de treinamento dos funcionários para a realização do teste de proveta, procedimento gratuito que permite ao consumidor verificar a qualidade da gasolina.

A fiscalização verificou, ainda, que o estabelecimento não fazia a drenagem do fundo do tanque de armazenamento de óleo diesel.

Outra irregularidade foi encontrada nas instalações elétricas em área classificada de risco: freezers com tomadas inadequadas estavam instalados a 1,20 metro das bombas medidoras, em desacordo com os requisitos de segurança previstos na norma.

Já no segundo posto de combustíveis foram constatadas duas irregularidades: a falta de treinamento dos funcionários para a realização do teste de proveta e a ausência de drenagem do fundo do tanque destinado ao armazenamento de óleo diesel.

Uma outra farmácia também foi autuada, mas não foi interditada. Foi apontada a ausência de informação sobre a proibição de exigir o CPF do consumidor como condição para a concessão de descontos no local.

articles.title: Venda de combustíveis em galões: MPF pede suspensão no Amazonas | G1
articles.standfirst: Medida deve valer enquanto durar a emergência provocada pelos incêndios. Agência Nacional do Petróleo, Gás Natural e Biocombustíveis e o governo estadual têm cinco dias para informar se vão seguir a recomendação.
articles.summary: MPF recomenda suspender a venda de combustíveis em galões no Amazonas para dificultar incêndios criminosos durante o período de emergência ambiental.
articles.body:
MPF recomendou a suspensão da venda de combustível em galão no Amazonas. — Foto: Divulgação/MPF

O Ministério Público Federal (MPF) recomendou à Agência Nacional do Petróleo, Gás Natural e Biocombustíveis (ANP) e ao governo do Amazonas que suspendam a venda de gasolina, etanol e diesel em galões, garrafas, bombonas e outros recipientes portáteis em todo o estado.

A medida deve valer enquanto durar a emergência provocada pelas queimadas e tem o objetivo de dificultar o transporte de combustíveis para provocar ou ampliar incêndios florestais.

A recomendação prevê que os combustíveis sejam vendidos diretamente nos tanques de veículos, embarcações, máquinas e equipamentos apresentados nos postos, incluindo os flutuantes.

A ANP e o governo estadual têm cinco dias, a partir do recebimento do documento, para informar por escrito se vão seguir a recomendação e quais medidas pretendem adotar. Caso decidam não acatá-la, deverão apresentar justificativas técnicas e jurídicas.

moradores de comunidades sem acesso por estrada ou sem postos de combustíveis;

e propriedades rurais cadastradas que precisem de diesel para abastecer máquinas agrícolas e geradores.

Nesses casos, a venda deverá seguir regras de controle, como identificação do comprador, registro da finalidade e da quantidade adquirida, uso de recipientes certificados e limites diários, conforme cada situação.

Segundo o MPF, a venda sem restrições e sem identificação do comprador pode facilitar o transporte de combustíveis para áreas de vegetação, margens de rios, várzeas e assentamentos sem acesso rodoviário. Isso dificultaria a fiscalização e poderia favorecer a ação de incendiários.

“Restringir essa venda, com exceções para quem realmente precisa, é a forma mais rápida de dificultar a ação dos incendiários”, afirma o procurador da República André Luiz Porreca Ferreira Cunha, autor da recomendação.

A recomendação também destaca que os postos não podem, por iniciativa própria, recusar ou limitar a venda de combustíveis em recipientes. Segundo o documento, as normas da ANP e o Código de Defesa do Consumidor impedem a recusa de venda nessas condições.

Por isso, o MPF defende que a restrição seja formalizada pela agência reguladora ou pelo governo estadual. A medida daria respaldo aos revendedores para negar a venda nos casos previstos, evitando multas e reclamações.

Dados do Instituto Nacional de Pesquisas Espaciais (Inpe) citados na recomendação apontam que o Amazonas registrou 3.726 focos de calor em setembro de 2026. O número representa um aumento de 295,5% em relação ao mesmo mês de 2025.

O governo do Amazonas já havia proibido o uso do fogo em todo o estado por 120 dias e decretado situação de emergência em 36 municípios. A medida foi reconhecida pelo governo federal.

A recomendação também cita uma avaliação do Ministério do Meio Ambiente e Mudança do Clima de que os incêndios têm origem humana intencional. O documento menciona ainda o reforço das investigações sobre uma possível atuação coordenada de incendiários.

MPF alerta para possíveis medidas judiciais

O MPF adverte que o descumprimento da recomendação poderá levar à adoção de medidas administrativas e judiciais. Entre as possibilidades está a apuração da responsabilidade pessoal de agentes públicos que deixarem de agir quando houver obrigação de fazê-lo.

O caso é acompanhado pelo 13º Ofício da Procuradoria da República no Amazonas, responsável pela atuação relacionada à prevenção e ao combate às queimadas.

articles.title: Moto com três pessoas e sem iluminação escapa por pouco de acidente | G1
articles.standfirst: Com base no Código de Trânsito Brasileiro (CTB), as infrações registradas no vídeo estão nos artigos 244 e 230 da legislação.
articles.summary: Com base no Código de Trânsito Brasileiro (CTB), as infrações registradas no vídeo estão nos artigos 244 e 230 da legislação.
articles.body:
Um motorista precisou desviar bruscamente de uma motocicleta que estava à sua frente na TO-335, na região de Couto Magalhães, no norte do estado. A lanterna de freio da moto estava apagada, e o veículo transportava três pessoas durante a noite. O flagrante foi registrado por uma câmera veicular, e o vídeo ganhou repercussão nas redes sociais nesta semana. (Veja vídeo acima).

📱 Clique aqui para seguir o canal do g1 TO no WhatsApp

As imagens foram registradas no noite do dia 9 de outubro. É possível ver o carro seguindo pela rodovia quando, de repente, a motocicleta surge na escuridão, a poucos metros de distância. O motorista, Júnior Silva, conseguiu reagir após um alerta da esposa, que estava no banco do passageiro. Logo após a manobra, o motociclista acionou a seta para sinalizar sua posição na via.

Júnior contou que comprou a câmera veicular recentemente para sua segurança pessoal, após ter sido vítima de uma batida em julho, quando o outro condutor fugiu do local. Ele relatou que, por um momento, o casal ficou em estado de choque com o susto.

"Foi a minha esposa quem percebeu a moto no meio da pista sem sinalização nenhuma. Foi um susto muito grande, nos causou tremores por alguns instantes. O impacto foi de imaginar o pior que poderia ter acontecido se eu tivesse batido neles ou se viesse um carro na pista ao contrário", disse Júnior.

De acordo com o Código de Trânsito Brasileiro (CTB), as infrações estão previstas nos artigos 244 e 230. Transportar passageiro fora do assento adequado é infração gravíssima, com multa de R$ 293,47 e sete pontos na CNH. Já conduzir o veículo com defeito no sistema de iluminação é infração média, com multa de R$ 130,16 e quatro pontos na CNH. Em ambos os casos, pode haver retenção do veículo, conforme as condições previstas na legislação.

Motorista conseguiu desviar de moto após aviso aos gritos da passageira — Foto: Reprodução/Colinas Notícias

Questionado sobre o uso do farol baixo no momento do susto, Júnior explicou que havia acabado de cruzar com outro veículo que vinha no sentido contrário e mudou a intensidade da luz para não ofuscar a visão do outro motorista.

“Vinha um carro na mão contrária, por isso eu abaixei o farol. Logo em seguida que o carro passou, foi onde aconteceu o susto. Graças a Deus, a minha mulher percebeu a tempo e evitamos o pior”, explicou.

O perito de trânsito Marco Aurélio afirma que esse tipo de ocorrência é frequente, apesar de o reparo do sistema de iluminação ter um custo considerado baixo.

“Uma ocorrência não tão rara de acontecer: colisão traseira por falta de visibilidade do veículo à frente, devido à falta de luz traseira! Problema extremamente barato de se sanar. Contudo, a negligência na manutenção ocasiona inúmeros acidentes, inclusive com óbitos”, afirmou.

articles.title: Hackers steal children's data after company used 'Password1' for old account
articles.summary: The data watchdog reprimanded Ogi Networks Limited and Data Cymru after the 2024 ransomware attack.
articles.body:
A cyber-attack stole information belonging to thousands of children by accessing an account that used the password "Password1", a data watchdog has said.

The Information Commission's Office (ICO) has reprimanded Ogi Networks Limited (ONL) and Data Cymru after the attack on 1 November 2024.

The hackers exposed personal information belonging to 3,300 people, mostly children, by using a test account, known as Test2, which had existed for more than 12 years and was protected by the password that could be compromised in less than a second.

ONL said the account "should have been removed long before criminals were able to use it", adding it had brought in independent cyber-security specialists.

The company, which provided IT services to Data Cymru, said it accepted the ICO's findings and had "acted on them".

Data Cymru merged with the Welsh Local Government Association (WLGA) in 2025, who said there was no evidence the stolen information was "shared further or misused".

ONL and Data Cymru were found to have breached UK GDPR rules by failing to properly protect their systems and by not regularly checking whether their security measures were effective.

During the ransomware attack, the hackers encrypted 182.7GB of data and stole 42GB from Data Cymru's systems. It exposed the personal information related to two projects supporting children and families.

David Doodson, head of investigations at the Information Commission's Office, said: "Password1 is not an appropriate password, it is a wide-open door to nefarious actors.

"This incident shows how a single weak password, attached to an account that was no longer needed, can leave the door open to a serious cyber-attack that can affect thousands."

Doodson added the responsibility for "these failures did not sit with one organisation alone".

According to the watchdog, ONL created a test account in 2012 and used the password "Password1" to protect it, failing to audit it or remove it for more than 12 years.

It also did not review local administrator accounts after they were first deployed, with accounts on three affected systems using the same password, for the same period of time.

The watchdog said Data Cymru failed to put a data protection agreement in place with ONL, and that there was a gap in responsibility between the two organisations.

It also said Data Cymru failed to ensure the dormant test account was identified and removed, or updated to meet stronger password requirements.

The ICO added it was a lesson for every organisation to "use strong passwords, protect remote access with multi-factor authentication, regularly review every user account, and be completely clear about who is responsible for cyber-security when services are outsourced".

Following the cyber-attack, both organisations introduced stronger security measures.

ONL introduced a process prompting customers to review active accounts periodically and providing recommendations about accounts that should be removed, the ICO said.

It also strengthened its account access controls, including the use of multi-factor authentication.

On 30 April 2025, Data Cymru and ONL entered into a legally compliant data processing contract.

Data Cymru also introduced periodic account reviews and strengthened account access controls, including using multi-factor authentication.

A spokesperson for ONL said: "Within a week of the attack, we'd worked with Data Cymru to check every account on its network and switched off the ones it no longer needed that same day.

"We also brought in independent cyber-security specialists to investigate."

They added: "Since then, we've protected remote access with multi-factor authentication and introduced regular account reviews for the customers whose networks we look after, so accounts that aren't needed are found and removed.

"This was limited to the server we hosted for Data Cymru. No other customer information held by ONL was affected."

A WLGA spokesperson said it remained "committed to maintaining robust information governance standards and continually reviewing the measures we have in place".

"We recognise the fundamental importance of strong information governance and of protecting the information entrusted to organisations working on behalf of local government.

"Since the incident, measures have been put in place to strengthen the arrangements identified by the ICO, including the removal of dormant user accounts, strengthened password and remote user access controls, and improved data processing arrangements to clearly define contractual responsibilities for security and audit activities," the spokesperson added.

articles.title: Brookings paper offers broad plan to shrink Fed balance sheet
articles.summary: Oct 21 (Reuters) - The Federal Reserve can substantially shrink its balance sheet if it overhauls its rate control toolkit to provide liquidity on demand, if...
articles.body:
Oct 21 (Reuters) - The Federal Reserve can substantially shrink its balance sheet if it overhauls its rate control toolkit to provide liquidity on demand, if those alterations are in made in conjunction with rule changes that allow banks to hold lower levels of cash on hand, says a new paper published by the Brookings ‌Institution.

The proposed roster of changes could allow the Fed to downsize overall holdings from their current $6.8 trillion level to around $4.5 trillion, with the proposed level of reserves in the financial ‌system ebbing from around the $3 trillion mark to around $1 trillion, wrote Chris Hughes, Nonresident Fellow at the think tank's Hutchins Center on Fiscal and Monetary Policy.

The paper argues now is the time to consider bold change given that new Fed Chairman Kevin ​Warsh wants a smaller Fed balance sheet and has named a task force to consider ways to make that happen.

"Opportunities to reset Fed operating systems do not come often," Hughes wrote, adding "this moment should not be wasted."

If done, "The Fed's footprint as a share of GDP would be smaller than at any point since 2008, and the interest paid to banks would fall by roughly two-thirds," Hughes wrote, alluding to Fed interest costs on its balance that have led the central bank into an unprecedented period of loss making.

The key to making this happen is moving away from the Fed's current system of so-called ample reserves, where it ‌aims to keep the financial system flush with large amounts of cash, ⁠with control of short-term rates delivered through a complicated toolkit and periodic waves of central bank bond buying.

The new system would be called "Elastic Reserves" and would be more responsive to market demand for cash, Hughes wrote.

The ample reserves system developed over the years following the global financial crisis, which kicked off nearly 20 ⁠years ago. The Fed's push then to near-zero interest rates drove it buy large amounts of bonds to provide economic stimulus and market stabilization.

The Fed again bought bonds in large numbers during the COVID-19 pandemic, and collectively those purchases drove overall central bank holdings from just under a trillion dollars to a peak of $9 trillion in 2022, before the central bank began passively reducing its bond holdings.

For many current Fed officials, while the levels of Fed ​holdings ​are large, ample reserves works in real world conditions. And a number of experts also reckon banks flush with ​cash are better prepared to deal with financial troubles when they arise.

articles.title: Investors ‘almost certainly’ in midst of AI bubble: Ken Griffin
articles.summary: Billionaire investor Ken Griffin said Tuesday that investors are dealing with an artificial intelligence bubble, as companies rack up debt to satisfy the demand for data centers and models. “There’s almost certainly bubbles within this moment in time. And any radical transformation of our economy is generally intertwined with a bubble,” Griffin, the founder of…
articles.body:
Billionaire investor Ken Griffin said Tuesday that investors are dealing with an artificial intelligence bubble , as companies rack up debt to satisfy the demand for data centers and models.

“There’s almost certainly bubbles within this moment in time. And any radical transformation of our economy is generally intertwined with a bubble,” Griffin, the founder of Citadel, told Bloomberg’s Dani Burger at his firm’s Future of Global Markets Conference.

The Citadel CEO noted that corporate America “has been very uneven in its ability to extract value” from AI models.

Debt owed by major tech companies has piled up this year, as the AI build-out marches on. The companies leading the build-out — Amazon, CoreWeave, Google, Meta, Microsoft and Oracle — had issued $193 billion in bonds as of early August, up from $16.7 billion in 2024, according to data from LSEG.

Looking ahead, investment in data centers, networking infrastructure and other equipment necessary for the AI build-out will total $10.3 trillion from last year to 2032, according to projections from the Brookings Institution.

Stocks have slid in recent weeks, as investors raise the caution flag about mounting debt totals. The Nasdaq composite dropped by more than 100 points over the last two weeks, while the S&P 500 has dipped by roughly 90 points during that time period.

“I think all of corporate America is looking at their bills from Anthropic and OpenAI and going, ‘OK, we need to think about how to make sure we’re getting productivity out of this,’” Griffin said Tuesday.

But the hedge fund manager and major GOP donor still has a positive outlook of the future, referencing the railroad boom as an example of a “giant technological” transformation that was “game-changing for the world.”

He added, “And the companies that are on the other side of that bubble are the market leaders for decades to come.”

articles.title: Polymarket blocks wagers on fate of Cornell students accused of sexual assault
articles.summary: After facing public backlash, Polymarket has removed a market that allowed users to wager on the fate of the seven Cornell University students accused of sexually assaulting a woman at a fraternity house in 2024. The prediction market archived the market, which asked whether any of the so-called Cornell 7 would be charged with a…
articles.body:
After facing public backlash, Polymarket has removed a market that allowed users to wager on the fate of the seven Cornell University students accused of sexually assaulting a woman at a fraternity house in 2024.

The prediction market archived the market, which asked whether any of the so-called Cornell 7 would be charged with a felony sex crime.

“Our primary goal at Polymarket is to bring objective, data-driven insight to the most important questions of our time,” a spokesperson said in a statement.

“This market addressed whether the government would take action — a process that deserves scrutiny, particularly in a case of such serious concern,” they continued. “That said, we believe in the wisdom of crowds, have heard them loud and clear, and removed the market.”

The market opened Sept. 30 and had nearly $400,000 in trading volume as of Oct. 4, according to a snapshot of the site earlier this month. The volume had reached more than $450,000 by the time the market was taken down, The Associated Press reported.

It appeared on Polymarket’s international site. The company has two platforms, a U.S.-based site that is regulated by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission and an international cryptocurrency-based site.

“This is a victory for survivors,” said Jenna Sherman, campaign director at UltraViolet, which is leading a petition for brand ambassadors to cut ties with the company.

“By allowing its users to gamble on the ‘Cornell 7’ case, Polymarket was essentially gamifying gang rape and profiting from the pain of courageous survivors like Jane Doe,” Sherman added in a statement.

A former Cornell student, who has chosen to remain anonymous, filed a lawsuit against seven fraternity members and the university last month over her alleged gang rape at the Chi Phi fraternity house in 2024.

The lawsuit has drawn scrutiny onto how Cornell and other universities handle campus sexual assault cases. Earlier this month, the Ithaca, N.Y., school brought in a former acting U.S. attorney general to conduct an independent review of its policies and practices related to sexual misconduct.

New York Gov. Kathy Hochul (D) has also appointed state Attorney General Letitia James to investigate the case.

articles.title: Meet the US’s newest national park, Chiricahua
articles.summary: The U.S. now has 64 national parks, four of which you’ll find in Arizona.
articles.body:
(NEXSTAR) – America has a new national park, bringing the nation’s tally of true national parks to 64.

President Trump on Tuesday signed H.R. 6380 , redesignating Chiricahua National Monument as the Chiricahua National Park.

Chiricahua is located about two hours east of Tucson in the southeast corner of Arizona, not far from Saguaro National Park, within the historical territory of the Chiricahua Apache tribes.

“Chiricahua’s towering rock spires, rich Apache heritage and remarkable biodiversity make it one of America’s most extraordinary landscapes,” Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum said in a press release . “This new designation will shine a national spotlight on one of Arizona’s hidden gems, creating opportunities to welcome more visitors, strengthen local economies and share this incredible landscape with more Americans.”

The site, sometimes referred to as the “Wonderland of Rocks,” was designated as a national monument in 1924, preserving the “rugged volcanic landscape, diverse wildlife, and cultural history” found within its roughly 12,000 acres. Elevating Chiricahua to national park status “reflects the national significance of the area’s natural and cultural resources and the longstanding efforts to conserve them,” Interior Department officials said Tuesday.

The Chiricahua Mountains, an inactive volcanic range, are also considered a sky island mountain range, meaning they protect the rare wildlife found within them. The newest national park is home to more than 1,000 plant species — many of which can only be found within its boundary — and numerous birds and mammals.

The area has evidence of thousands of years of human use, according to the park service. That spans from prehistoric peoples to Buffalo Soldiers — or the Black U.S. troops who were stationed at the monument site after the Civil War, during a government campaign against Apache leaders Geronimo and Cochise.

President Calvin Coolidge named the site a national monument in 1924 under the federal Antiquities Act. President Franklin D. Roosevelt expanded it in 1938. House lawmakers approved the park’s redesignation in a voice vote in March. The Senate passed it Sept. 30 by unanimous consent.

National monuments are designed to protect specific locations and objects, such as archaeological or historical sites, whereas national parks have a broader purpose including recreation and the preservation of vast expanses of wilderness. Parks and monuments alike are managed by the National Park Service.

Chiricahua is the first new national park since 2021, when New River Gorge National Park and Preserve in West Virginia was similarly redesignated. This marks Arizona’s fourth national park, alongside Saguaro, Petrified Forest, and the Grand Canyon — though, technically, all sites overseen by the National Park Service are collectively called “parks.” Arizona has 22 total sites by that count.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: Why political texts keep coming even after you block them
articles.summary: George Weiner built PACspam.org to trace who sends nonstop political fundraising texts after blocking numbers repeatedly failed to stop the messages.
articles.body: Your phone buzzes. Another political text. This time, it's an urgent fundraising appeal claiming a campaign desperately needs your help before midnight. You delete it, block the number and get on with your day. Then tomorrow, another one arrives from a completely different number. Sound familiar? I've been there, and frankly, I'm fed up with it. On "The CyberGuy Report" podcast, I sat down with George Weiner, founder of PACspam.org and head of the digital agency Whole Whale. George got so frustrated with the relentless political texts that he created a free tool to help people figure out who's sending them. Our conversation revealed why blocking numbers often gets you nowhere, how political fundraising has become a lucrative business and what you can do to fight back. FIVE DATA BROKER OPT-OUT MYTHS THAT LEAVE RETIREES EXPOSED Join our upcoming CyberGuy LIVE class: 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money In this free live online class, Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson will share five practical ways to protect your trip and your wallet this holiday travel season. You’ll learn how to secure your phone and personal information, find better travel deals, avoid common scams, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed. Join us Saturday, October 31, at 11 AM ET / 8 AM PT. Register free now at CyberGuyLive.com. Why blocking political text messages doesn't work You would think blocking a phone number would send a pretty clear message. Apparently, political texting operations don't always take the hint. I asked George why texts from the same political groups kept showing up after I blocked their numbers. "Well, you block one number, and you've only blocked one number," Weiner explained. He introduced me to a technique called snowshoeing, which allows an organization to spread its messages across multiple phone numbers. A single campaign or political action committee (PAC) may use many different numbers to reach the same people. So, even after you block one sender, another number can deliver the next fundraising appeal. For George, this frustration became personal. As a father of three, he worries about missing an important call from his children's school. "That could be the school, right? That could be an emergency," he explained. Instead, his phone often interrupts him with another fundraising appeal. He tried replying STOP, reporting messages and registering for the National Do Not Call Registry. Yet the interruptions continued. "I have done it all, and I still get these messages," Weiner said. That raises a question I've been asking for years. How did these organizations get our phone numbers in the first place? How political campaigns get your phone number You might assume a campaign needs your permission before adding your number to its texting list. Unfortunately, political outreach operates under rules that leave plenty of room for unsolicited messages. Weiner explained how phone numbers can circulate through political donor and voter databases. Campaigns may also combine registration information with commercially available data to identify potential supporters. Furthermore, organizations can purchase or exchange contact lists, allowing your information to reach groups you've never heard of. Voter registration records vary by state, and phone numbers aren't necessarily public in those records. However, organizations can match voter information with other databases to build detailed contact profiles. Political donations can create additional exposure. As we've previously reported, federal political contribution records can reveal personal information, including your name and address, when disclosure requirements apply. Once your number enters this fundraising network, tracking every organization that holds it becomes extremely difficult. The money behind nonstop political fundraising texts Here's something from my conversation with George that really caught my attention. There's a substantial amount of money flowing through the political texting business, and the people sending these messages have financial reasons to keep doing it. Weiner pointed to approximately $65 million spent on political texting services during the 2024 election cycle, based on his analysis of Federal Election Commission records. He also believes 2026 spending could exceed that amount, although a final election-cycle total isn't yet available. George also highlighted how much money individual political messaging vendors receive. According to PACspam's analysis of FEC records covering December 2008 through May 2026, reported payments totaled $17 million for Switchboard, $14.4 million for Mothership Strategies and $10.6 million for Message Digital. These figures span multiple election cycles and reflect reported payments to political messaging vendors, which may include services beyond texting. Why political fundraising texts keep coming "There is money to be made," Weiner told me. He explained that fundraising operations can keep paying to send messages as long as the donations they generate justify the expense. Even a small percentage of people responding with money can make another round of texts financially worthwhile. Some appeals claim a donation deadline is approaching or suggest a candidate faces an immediate financial emergency. Others use provocative headlines designed to make you react before thinking. Weiner also raised concerns about how much money some PACs actually direct toward candidates. He pointed to investigations suggesting that certain organizations spend heavily on fundraising while relatively little reaches the candidate being promoted. PACs operate under different rules, however, and not all are established to make direct candidate contributions. That's why it's important to investigate where your donation will go. And this problem crosses political lines. Weiner stressed that organizations associated with different political parties use these tactics. The repeated pleas for money, he believes, can end up alienating the very voters campaigns want to reach. That brings us to an interesting way to investigate who's behind the messages. How PACspam helps identify who's sending political texts George created PACspam.org to give people more information about the organizations filling their phones with unsolicited political messages. "Our phones don't have to live like this," Weiner said while explaining why he built the tool. The free service analyzes political fundraising texts and attempts to identify the committee behind them. It can examine fundraising links and use public campaign finance information to help trace the organization responsible. PACspam also helps document complaints and tracks repeat offenders using information connected to FEC-registered committees. Its public leaderboard focuses on texting behavior rather than political affiliation. Meanwhile, its FEC Texting-Spend Explorer lets visitors investigate campaign spending on texting services. In some cases, PACspam can also help identify the texting technology provider that delivered the message. That last part is particularly interesting because those technology companies may serve multiple political organizations. Rather than contacting only the committee asking for money, Weiner suggests contacting the texting platform when it can be identified. "They do answer," Weiner told me when I asked whether these companies respond to complaints. He described receiving a response from the legal department of a texting provider. That company explained how he could request placement on its own do-not-contact list. The approach could be more useful than blocking one phone number because it targets a provider that may handle messages for multiple political organizations. Still, one company's removal list won't necessarily apply to competing platforms. Of course, results can vary. An organization may use another platform, and some messages don't contain enough information to identify the sender. Still, contacting a texting provider offers another avenue to pursue. DEM FUNDRAISING GIANT ACTBLUE ACCUSED OF FRAUDULENT DONATION 'COVER-UP' IN EXPLOSIVE REPORT How to use PACspam.org Getting started requires only a political text you've received. Here's what to do. PACspam can prepare complaint information and help document unwanted political messages, but it doesn't automatically send those complaints on your behalf. It also cannot guarantee that your number will disappear from political texting lists. I also asked George an important privacy question. What happens to the information people submit? "We're not collecting your number. I just want that message," he said. According to Weiner, you don't need an account to use PACspam. Whole Whale also says uploaded screenshots are processed and discarded, while personal messages aren't displayed publicly. Those are the service's stated privacy practices, so I still recommend removing identifying details before submitting anything. Are unsolicited political text messages legal? Here's where things get frustrating. The Federal Communications Commission treats political texts differently depending on how they're sent. Political messages sent through an automatic telephone dialing system generally require prior express consent before reaching your cellphone. However, messages sent manually through peer-to-peer texting systems can fall outside those restrictions. That helps explain why so many campaign texts can reach people who never specifically requested them. The National Do Not Call Registry generally doesn't cover political outreach either. So, registering your number may reduce some telemarketing calls without stopping political fundraising appeals. The FCC also says political campaigns should honor opt-out requests when recipients reply STOP. For robotexts covered by federal consent rules, revocation requests must generally be honored within 10 business days. However, an opt-out from one sender won't necessarily remove your number from other political organizations' databases. 5 ways to block political text messages and protect yourself You may not be able to eliminate every political text, but several steps can reduce the interruptions and help protect your information. 1. Reply STOP when you recognize the sender If you receive a message from a legitimate political campaign or organization, replying STOP can unsubscribe you from that sender's messages. However, be selective. If the text looks suspicious or contains an unfamiliar fundraising link, avoid responding. Scammers sometimes impersonate political organizations, and engaging with suspicious messages may confirm that your number is active. 2. Turn on spam filtering on your phone Your smartphone already has tools that can help move unwanted messages out of your main inbox. Here's where to find them. On iPhone running iOS 27: Unknown senders can move into a separate folder, reducing interruptions. If needed, tap Allow Notifications to choose which categories of unknown messages can still alert you. Availability varies by region. On Google Pixel or Samsung Galaxy using Google Messages: Google Messages can flag suspicious texts and move some of them into the Spam & blocked folder. Menu options may vary by device and app version. Remember to review your filtered messages occasionally so important texts don't get overlooked. FCC ROBOCALL CRACKDOWN COULD CHANGE PHONE PRIVACY 3. Block and report repeat senders Blocking individual numbers can reduce messages from persistent senders, even though other numbers may still get through. On an iPhone, open the unwanted conversation, tap the sender's icon, select Info and choose Block Contact. On an iPhone, reporting a message as spam doesn't automatically block the sender. You need to block the contact separately if you want messages from that number stopped. On Google Messages, touch and hold the unwanted conversation, then tap Block. You can also select Report spam before confirming. For additional guidance, see our guide to blocking phone numbers and texts. 4. Report unwanted texts to your carrier and the FCC You can forward unwanted political texts to 7726, which spells SPAM on a telephone keypad. This alerts your wireless carrier and can help its spam detection efforts. For suspected violations of federal calling or texting rules, you can also submit a complaint through the FCC Consumer Complaint Center. If the text appears to be a scam, report it to the Federal Trade Commission at reportfraud.ftc.gov/. Keep a screenshot of the suspicious message if you may need it for your report. 5. Donate directly and limit your personal data exposure One of George's strongest recommendations involves political donations. If you want to support a candidate, find that candidate's official website yourself rather than following a link in an unsolicited text. During our interview, George warned that donating through unfamiliar political fundraising texts can encourage additional solicitations. He described how a successful donation might lead organizations to think, "We got one, let's send twice as many messages." His recommendation was straightforward: Give through the candidate's official website instead of an unsolicited fundraising link. That helps you verify who is receiving your money. However, even donating directly can lead to additional campaign messages, so review the site's privacy disclosures and contact preferences. Additionally, consider limiting how widely your phone number appears online. Data brokers can collect and resell personal information, and removing your details from covered sites may reduce future exposure. Check out my top picks for data removal services and get a free scan to find out if your personal information is already out on the web by visiting CyberGuy.com. Keep in mind that commercial data removal services cannot erase legally required public campaign finance records. They also can't guarantee removal from every political organization's contact database. Kurt's key takeaways What struck me most about my conversation with George is how much money is being made from messages that so many of us desperately want to stop. We block numbers and ask to be removed, yet the texts keep coming. And the organizations making money from this system have little incentive to change it. I appreciate that George decided to do something about it. His PACspam tool offers a way to investigate who's behind these messages and push back through official complaint channels. I'd love to see political organizations become more accountable for how they use our personal information. After all, supporting a candidate shouldn't mean giving every fundraising operation unlimited access to your phone. Want to hear exactly how George is fighting back? Listen to my full interview with George Weiner on The CyberGuy Report podcast. We dig deeper into the political texting business, the companies behind it and what you can do when blocking numbers fails. articles.title: Pennsylvania warns doctors about rising rates of rare congenital measles
articles.summary: The Pennsylvania health department issued a warning to doctors Monday about an increase in measles cases during pregnancy, along with rising concern about congenital measles, a disease rarely seen in the U.S. The department’s alert said congenital measles — a measles infection in a newborn contracted from the mother — was identified “for the first…
articles.body:
The Pennsylvania health department issued a warning to doctors Monday about an increase in measles cases during pregnancy, along with rising concern about congenital measles, a disease rarely seen in the U.S.

The department’s alert said congenital measles — a measles infection in a newborn contracted from the mother — was identified “for the first time in decades.”

There are more than 1,200 measles cases in Pennsylvania, and the health department has confirmed five deaths, though a sixth death was reported earlier this month in Franklin County.

Few pediatricians have treated a newborn with congenital measles, presenting a clinical challenge for physicians.

In response to rising cases, the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) added a “frequently asked questions” page about congenital measles to its website in September.

According to the AAP, an estimated 25 percent to 30 percent of babies with mothers who have a measles infection at birth are also infected. Only measles infections that occur in the last two weeks of pregnancy or the first 10 days postdelivery are considered congenital.

Congenital measles was uncommon in the U.S. before the measles vaccine was introduced in the early 1960s because most women had been infected as children. But as vaccination rates plummet and measles outbreaks become more common, congenital measles is making a comeback.

In its alert, the Pennsylvania health department urged women to get the measles, mumps, rubella vaccine (MMR) before pregnancy. MMR is not recommended once pregnancy begins because it is a live virus vaccine.

Contracting measles while pregnant increases the risk of miscarriage, early labor and low birth weight, the department said. Babies who contract measles before or during birth can also become very sick and are at risk for health complications later in life.

Nonimmune pregnant women and babies who are exposed to measles have a six-day window where they can be given immunoglobulin, which can provide protection against measles infection or reduce the risk of serious illness among susceptible people.

Still, vaccination is the best way to prevent measles. If exposure happens to a pregnant woman who received the two-dose MMR series, she should be protected against the virus.

articles.title: Elon Musk has a bold answer to America’s $40 trillion debt crisis
articles.summary: Elon Musk says that DOGE proved Washington will not cut its way out of the deficit.
articles.body:
Elon Musk says the United States will not fix its national debt by cutting spending, and that "AI and robots" are the only real way out, according to an exclusive interview with Axios.

The national debt stood at roughly $40.39 trillion on Oct, 15, Treasury data shows.

Musk made the remarks in conversation with biographer Walter Isaacson for a new podcast. He said the DOGE experiment he once led showed the deficit cannot be solved from inside government, because almost no one in authority wants to cut spending .

"If you try to solve the deficit and stop wasteful spending, you make a lot of enemies," Musk said.

"The only way we're going to solve the national debt is with AI and robots," Musk added. During the interview he said that he should have "focused" on AI sooner than he did.

"We're not gonna solve it by trying to save our way there," he said.

Musk added that President Donald Trump "likes to be liked" , and that cutting waste makes enemies. He also admitted he "kinda got carried away" at DOGE, stayed away from his companies too long, and should have returned to AI sooner.

The comments came two days before Musk pledged to give every American child one SpaceX share next year.

This is not the first time Musk has suggested that AI and robots could help solve the U.S. debt problem.

In a podcast interview in Nov, 2025, Musk said AI and robotics were "pretty much the only thing" that could solve the U.S. debt crisis. Musk called the debt "insanely high," pointing out that interest payments alone exceeded the entire U.S. military budget.

He argued that AI would eventually push the output of goods and services past growth in the money supply, likely causing "deflation".

His timeline was three years. He admitted, however, that AI had not yet lifted productivity enough to get there.

The 10-year Treasury yield climbed to 5.29% in late September, while the 30-year yield hit 5.61%, its highest level since 2002 .

Bitcoin has long been pitched as a hedge against exactly this kind of sovereign debt.

Musk's plan comes with a twist. Musk has said that if AI and robots increase output , the government must issue dollars to people or face "massive disinflation."

articles.title: Musk: SpaceX, Tesla merger a ‘good idea’
articles.summary: Elon Musk said Tuesday that his two companies, SpaceX and Tesla, have formed independent special committees to discuss the potential merger, calling it “a good idea.” “I think it would be a good ​idea, but it’s really up to the special committees of both companies,” Musk told investors on a conference call, according to a…
articles.body:
Elon Musk said Tuesday that his two companies, SpaceX and Tesla, have formed independent special committees to discuss the potential merger, calling it “a good idea.”

“I think it would be a good ​idea, but it’s really up to the special committees of both companies,” Musk told investors on a conference call, according to a Reuters report . “Because I’m a conflicted party, I can’t actually be in ​the discussions of the special committees.”

Musk said the special committees were established by both companies at the request of shareholders, ⁠who would ultimately need to approve a deal. He added the committees had not agreed on transaction terms and may never do so, Reuters reported.

He added there is “a lot of merit” to combining the two companies, “as we are pretty much in the superintelligence singularity, and there’s a lot to be gained from ​cooperating on developing superintelligence software, chip design, the Terafab obviously, robotics, mass-to-orbit with the Starmind constellation, connectivity.”

Musk said in the call that the chip manufacturing joint venture, Terafab, should produce its first test chip sometime around May or June and aims to reach volume production.

SpaceX shares went up by more than 8 percent and Tesla shares rose more than 2 percent Wednesday morning following the reports of the possible merger, according to CNN .

Musk has been in the headlines after Ukraine’s military faced restricted access to Starshield, the military version of Starlink, earlier this month .

The Wall Street Journal reported that Musk ordered the slowdown, citing U.S. officials and people familiar with the matter, prompting calls for an investigation from several Democrats.

Musk initially claimed in a post to the social platform X that only President Trump had the ability to order the slowdown, adding that while Starlink is under Musk’s SpaceX, Starshield is owned and operated by the U.S. government.

The disruption impacted the capabilities of Ukraine’s drones, airplanes and helicopters.
